citationText: 16 Negative film has significant “exposure latitude;” which is generally exploited more than the latitude available in video cameras; hence during or after telecine transfer it may be necessary to expand part of the recovered density range of an over- or under-exposed negative to yield a satisfactory grey scale. This will also expand any quantising errors resulting from an insufficient number of amplitude coding levels. Where this grey scale correction is deferred (e.g. in so-called “tape-to-tape” colour correction), all equipment prior to this correction must maintain this larger dynamic range.
